conviction_note: Small positive lean: peers that reported after Wipro last spoke (TCS +0.5% cc q/q, HCLTech +2.3% cc q/q, Accenture +7% LC against a 1-5% guide) and Wipro's own July statement that large-deal decisions slipped into Q2, plus ADR shorts up ~63% since mid-August. Against that: the sector already rallied (+7.5% ADR in 5 days), Wipro has sold three of its last four prints, a seasonally weak Q3 guide is expected, and the Alpha Net contracts some brokers modelled had not closed. p_up 53 x abs 4.5 gives +0.27; impact_sum +0.8 is larger because each finding is sized alone and the sector run-up and this name's habit of selling prints act through p_up, not by shrinking the findings to match.
bar: Company guide: Q2 FY27 IT services revenue $2.574-2.627bn, -1.5% to +0.5% q/q cc, including a full quarter of Mindsprint (Q1 FY27 call transcript, 2026-07-16, https://www.wipro.com/content/dam/nexus/en/investor/quarterly-results/2026-2027/q1fy27/q1fy27-earnings-transcript.pdf). Street: IT services -0.5% to -1.4% q/q cc (MOFSL -0.5% incl ~0.7% Mindsprint inorganic; JM -0.5% cc; Nuvama -1%; Jefferies -1.4%; Emkay -1% USD), EBIT margin +20-50bp q/q (MOFSL to 16.4%), PAT Rs3,335-3,410cr, Q3 guide expected -2% to 0% (Emkay, Nuvama) or -1.5% to +0.5% (Jefferies). Sources: https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/wipro-q2-fy27-results-preview/ (2026-10-14) and https://www.tradingview.com/news/moodys:ab25a0f6a0c64:0-wipro-q2-preview-brokerages-expect-weak-revenue-growth-margin-recovery/ (undated, pre-print). Both previews agree and match the company guide, so the bar is sourced.
positioning_check: WIT ADR short interest 102,750,718 sh at the 2026-09-30 settlement (-0.9M vs 09-15), up from 62.96M at 08-14 and 84.54M at 08-31, so +63% over Aug-Sep. Days to cover 14.18 on 7.24M ADR ADV (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/wit/short-interest, read 2026-10-14). That is ~1.0% of the 9.89bn total shares; the share of ADR float could not be sourced. Some of it may be ADR/ordinary arbitrage rather than directional. No usable skew: the front chain (2026-10-16) is not two-sided; put/call OI 3.42 on only 615 contracts total. ADR run-up +7.49% over 5d and +6.85% over 20d, -41% from the 52-week high, +11% off the low.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Wipro's July guide printed above their own lines: TCS Q2 FY27 cc revenue +0.5% q/q with BFSI +2.5% (Oct 8), HCLTech +2.3% q/q cc with bookings +27% y/y and the low end of FY27 guidance firmed (Oct 12), Accenture Q4 LC +7% against a 1-5% guide with stock +~20% (Oct 1). The Wipro street bar is a -0.5% to -1.4% cc decline, the lower half of its -1.5% to +0.5% guide, so the read-through points to the middle or upper half of that range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wipro has sold its prints: Q3 FY26 (Jan 2026) -9.7% in India on one-offs and the outlook (https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/business/2026/01/19/wipro-shares-tumble-nearly-10-pc-post-q3-numbers.html); Q4 FY26 (Apr 2026) ADR -2.2% to -3%, India -4% on a -2% to 0% guide despite a buyback (https://www.outlookbusiness.com/markets/wipro-shares-slip-4-after-q4-brokerages-flag-concerns-despite-buyback); Q1 FY27 (Jul 2026) India +1.77% on a revenue miss with a -1.5% to +0.5% guide (https://www.indiainfoline.com/news/companies/wipro-q1-fy27-results-profit-rises-marginally-margins-fall-to-15-quarter-low-stock-gains-1-77). The reported quarter has mattered less than the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced at the sector level: Nifty IT rose more than 1,000 points on Oct 9 and Wipro +~3% (https://www.theweek.in/news/biz-tech/2026/10/09/nifty-it-up-more-than-1000-points-three-reasons-it-stocks-are-rallying-today.html), and the ADR is +7.5% over 5 days. What is not yet in the Wipro-specific estimates: the brokerage previews dated Oct 14 still sit at -0.5% to -1.4% cc, below the guide midpoint. If the peer read had reached Wipro's own numbers, those previews would sit at the guide midpoint or above.
findings.independence: HCLTech (https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/hcltech-q2-fy27-results-revenue-profit-and-deal-wins/, 2026-10-12) and Accenture (https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/company--news/accenture-shares-jump-as-q4-results-beat-own-guidance, ~2026-10-01) are separate documents. All three are proxies for Wipro, not Wipro's own number.

findings.finding: On the Q1 FY27 call (Jul 16) management said some large-deal decisions 'have actually slipped to quarter two', the pipeline is 'healthy', BFSI client insourcing 'is behind us' and BFSI Americas is ramping. Q1 total bookings were $3.37bn and large deals $1.63bn (13 deals), down sharply y/y. So Q2 bookings and large-deal TCV are set up to rebound, against PL Research's $2.7-2.8bn deal-win estimate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bookings have not carried Wipro on their own. Q2 FY26 (Oct 2025) had large-deal TCV of $2.9bn (+90% y/y) and the stock still fell on a weak guide (https://ticker.finology.in/discover/market-update/wipro-q2-fy26-results-analysis-deal-wins).
findings.why_not_priced: Public since July and inside management's own framing, so mostly expected. The PL $2.7-2.8bn estimate sits below Q1's $3.37bn even though the deals that slipped should land in Q2. If the slippage were priced, estimates would sit above Q1's bookings rather than below.
findings.independence: Same company document as the guide in the bar. HCLTech's +27% bookings is a separate peer signal that deal flow was live in the quarter (https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/hcltech-q2-fy27-results-revenue-profit-and-deal-wins/).

findings.finding: Completion of the Alpha Net Consulting contract acquisition (up to $70.8m; contracts generated $37.3m of revenue in 2025, ~$9m a quarter or ~0.35% of Wipro IT services) was pushed a second time, from Sep 30 to Dec 31, 2026, so it should contribute nothing to Q2. JM Financial's Q2 estimate assumes ~40bp from Alpha Net and Emkay's dollar estimate includes it, so those two may print ~0.3-0.4% below on reported dollars even though organic revenue is on their line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction on an acquisition-timing gap. Wipro's guide does not break out inorganic contribution ('We're not breaking our guidance out', Q1 call), so the effect is inside the guided range.
findings.why_not_priced: The Oct 14 preview (https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/wipro-q2-fy27-results-preview/) still carries JM's ~40bp Alpha Net contribution. If the deferral had been absorbed, that estimate would exclude it. It is small, inside the guide, and the other brokers (MOFSL, Nuvama) do not appear to rely on it.
findings.independence: Conflicts with a Zerodha/PUBT brief dated Jul 16 saying the deal had closed (https://www.zerodha.com/markets/stocks/NSE/WIPRO/). The later Sep 30 report of a second extension is taken as current. No primary exchange filing was opened.

findings.finding: The US Department of Labor suspended Wipro (with TCS, Infosys, HCL, Cognizant, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe) from the PERM green-card programme from Oct 8, with no end date. Wipro had 523 PERM approvals in FY25. This is a possible call topic on onsite hiring costs, but small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The sector rallied on Oct 9, the day after, with Nasscom saying the firms had already cut H-1B reliance (https://www.theweek.in/news/biz-tech/2026/10/09/nifty-it-up-more-than-1000-points-three-reasons-it-stocks-are-rallying-today.html).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is public, sector-wide, and the market shrugged it off. What remains is any cost or onsite-delivery comment on the Oct 15 call.

findings.finding: WIT ADR short interest rose from 62.96M shares (Aug 14) to 103.6M (Sep 15) and 102.75M (Sep 30), 14.18 days to cover on ADR volume. That is short positioning built into a print whose bar is already a decline, so a guide no worse than feared has a squeeze mechanism on the ADR.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No ADR-specific squeeze history sourced. The ADR fell 2.2-3% on the Apr 2026 weak guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The ADR's +7.5% 5-day run-up may already be partly covering. The Oct 15 settlement is not published until Oct 26. Some of the short may be ADR/ordinary arbitrage, which would not squeeze on news.
findings.independence: none. A single short-interest source (FINRA via Equibles).

outside_window.finding: Alpha Net contract acquisition now scheduled to complete by 2026-12-31, adding ~$9m a quarter of inorganic revenue from Q4 FY27 at the earliest.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew or implied move, and its history is 6-K noise. The lean is mildly positive and agrees with the run-up (+7.5% in 5d), which is the main reason it is small: the peer read is already in the sector price, and Wipro's own history is to sell the print on the guide.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction; Wipro has sold 3 of its last 4 prints): peer read-through +0.6 -> +0.4 and p_up 54 -> 53.
Lesson 6 (inside the company's guide): Alpha Net gap -0.3 -> -0.2 because it lands inside the guided range. The bar was verified to the company guide plus two agreeing preview sources, so no cap.
Lesson 6 / core table (already told by the company): deal-slippage bookings +0.5 -> +0.3 because management said it on the July call.
Lesson 7: short interest looked up before the negatives. The PERM and Alpha Net negatives were already small and were left as they were.
Base-rate lesson (untrusted FPI history): abs_move rebuilt from confirmed releases (-9.7%, ~-3%/-4%, +1.8%) rather than the baseline's 0.54%. This was already done in the draft.
